caption: Figure 11.5: Stabilized Leapfrog–Chebyshev Local Time Stepping (UnstructuredFIT2D(lts=2), Diaz & Grote 2009). Left: on a spatially graded mesh (h_max / h_min ≥ 2), only the narrow band of fine nodes F next to the scatterer (3–23% of the nodes, outside the outer radial PML and with σ = 0) takes sub-steps. Right: during each step, coarse nodes advance by 1.94× the global step while the fine band F takes 2 damped Chebyshev sub-steps (lts=2), conserving an exact discrete energy (drift 2×10⁻¹⁴ over 10⁵ steps) and halving total steps on B2 and B3.
visual_intent:
Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: primary grid G and its quantities in blue, dual grid G-tilde and its quantities in orange, exact/topological items in dark grey, approximate/material items in green, failure or warning items in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

Two panels side by side. LEFT PANEL (48% width) headed 'Spatial partition: fine band F vs. coarse nodes': Draw a 2D graded unstructured mesh around a circular scatterer (or narrow dimer gap). Shade the narrow collar of tiny triangles immediately surrounding the interface in orange, labelled 'fine nodes F (3–23% of the nodes, h_max / h_min ≥ 2): 2 Chebyshev substeps'. Shade the scatterer interior and the outer graded mesh in light blue, labelled 'coarse nodes (cylinder included): 1.94× the global step'. Shade the outermost ring in light grey labelled 'outer radial PML (excluded from F; σ = 0 in F)'. RIGHT PANEL (52% width) headed 'Time-stepping schedule: lts=1 (global leapfrog) vs. lts=2 (Leapfrog–Chebyshev)': Top timeline labelled 'Global leapfrog (lts=1)' in red/grey: all nodes march in small steps of size 'Δt_global'. Bottom timeline labelled 'Stabilized LTS (lts=2, Diaz & Grote 2009)' in blue/orange: coarse nodes (blue circles) take one large step of length '1.94× the global step', while fine nodes F (orange squares) take '2 damped Chebyshev substeps (lts=p)'. Below the timelines, display three badges exact to the manual: green 'exact discrete energy: drift 2×10⁻¹⁴ over 10⁵ steps', grey 'exact discrete adjoint: dot-product test < 10⁻¹⁴', and blue 'B2 / B3: 2× fewer steps with unchanged error (≈ 1.75× median wall-time speedup)'.
